evidence: Quint. 7.9.10: accūsātīvī geminātiōne facta amphibolia solvitur ablātīvō (locus in Lewis & Short s.v. accūsātīvus; wording not checked)
terms.comment: Short for cāsus accūsātīvus, a mistranslation of Greek αἰτιατική, as if it were the case of the accused; Varro also says cāsus accūsandī. A verb that takes the accusative accūsātīvō adjungitur (Traupman 239).

phrases.latin: accūsātīvī geminātiōne facta amphibolia solvitur ablātīvō
phrases.english: an ambiguity made by doubling the accusative is resolved by the ablative
phrases.source: Quint. 7.9.10 (locus in Lewis & Short; wording not checked)

phrases.english: For the verb canō takes the accusative.
This verb takes the accusative case.
